copy.chaplet.description: The chaplet of Saint Charbel: its red, white, and blue beads, the Father of Truth prayer, and how to pray it step by step, as described by St. Joseph Maronite Catholic Church.
copy.chaplet.text1: The chaplet of Saint Charbel is a short devotional prayer on beads: five sets of three beads - three red, one white, one blue - divided by five black beads, with a medal of the saint. It opens with the "Father of Truth" prayer which, according to the accounts cited by the Maronite Research Institute, he was praying when he was struck down at the altar.
copy.chaplet.text2: A chaplet is a small devotion prayed on a short string of beads - shorter than the Rosary, and shaped around a particular saint or mystery. The chaplet of Saint Charbel honors the hermit of Annaya through the things that defined him: his monastic vows, his love of the Eucharist, and his devotion to the Mother of God. The form described here follows the description published by
copy.chaplet.text3: - the prayer of the Maronite Divine Liturgy which, according to the accounts cited by the Maronite Research Institute, Saint Charbel was praying when he collapsed at his altar.
copy.chaplet.text4: According to the accounts cited by the Maronite Research Institute, this is the prayer Saint Charbel was reciting at the altar on December 16, 1898, when a stroke struck him during the Divine Liturgy. He died eight days later on December 24, the eve of Christmas - which is why the chaplet begins with this prayer.
copy.chaplet.text5: Maronite Research Institute: Saint Sharbel, citing Chebli (1950) and Awwad (1952) for the December 1898 illness and altar-prayer account
copy.litany.description: The Litany of Saint Charbel: twenty-nine invocations to the hermit of Annaya, a traditional form, and how to pray it alone or with a group.
copy.litany.text1: A traditional form. Prayed aloud, the italic lines are the response; praying alone, let each one land before moving on.
copy.litany.text2: Lord, infinitely Holy and glorified in Saint Charbel, grant us the grace of loving and serving You, following his example. Hear our petitions, through his intercession, and deliver us from all evil of body and soul. Amen.
copy.litany.text3: Charbel's Friends: Litany of Saint Charbel - a traditional form of the twenty-nine invocations and the closing collect
